cells.tense: What was given is visible now, and the giving is complete.
cells.ask: Keep tending one thing you have already built, on the same schedule, for a month — and note the day the care starts to feel like holding on.
cells.core:
The work is done and it is being seen. You know what you gave and you can look at the shape it has taken without flinching. What you released has become something that stands without you in the room, and the people around it know what it cost.

That does not mean it runs without you. It means you can feed what comes next without guarding what came before. Care that does not exhaust looks like this: you show up for the thing, you let it change, you do not grip. The risk here is that tending turns into clutching, and the sign is small — you stop being able to imagine it without you. When that shows up, put the weight down and let the thing keep standing.
cells.sheetLine: What you gave is visible and you have let it stand.
cells.verb: letting the work reach the people it was for
cells.place: in the shape of a thing, past the object it arrived in

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a judgment that has not been made yet.
cells.ask: Choose the part you keep returning to, spend ten minutes naming what you would change, and stop there for the day.
cells.core:
You are ahead of the room. The work is not yet in front of anyone, and you have already weighed it against a standard nobody has applied. Some part of it reads as insufficient, so no version gets to stand.

The attention is real. But anticipating a grade that has not been given is not the same as fixing anything. Ten minutes of naming what you would change gets you to a floor you can stand on, whether or not the room ever measures it. The practice does not have to feel certain. It has to stop scanning for a verdict that has not been issued — and when the refinement serves the work instead of the worry, it gets quieter on its own.

cells.tense: You built something and stepped back before anyone could see it.
cells.ask: Send one finished piece to one person who had no part in making it, with no explanation, this week.
cells.core:
Something you made is sitting in a room that did not get to answer. What happened to it got tied to the work itself, and now the last stretch is where you stop — send it, post it, bring it up, and something holds you in place.

The doing is not the missing part. The missing part is a hand other than yours reaching the thing. Send one finished piece to one person who had nothing to do with making it, and do not explain it after. What comes back does not have to settle anything for you. It only has to arrive, and the next time you carry something to the edge, the edge will already know your weight. The crossing is passable, and you have walked it once.

cells.tense: You are making the choices and describing them as the situation being what it is.
cells.ask: Before one task today, say out loud who the work is for and what showing up for them asks of you.
cells.core:
You are sorting what to keep and what to let go, deciding what a good outcome looks like, managing how the result gets described — without naming any of it. The work is happening. What is not happening is any acknowledgment that someone is steering it.

Going well, this looks like being able to say what you chose and why, and letting that be a choice rather than something that happened to you. Saying the shape out loud does not overstate it. Before one ordinary task today, say who the work is for and what showing up for them asks of you. That stays true whether or not anyone thanks you, and it gives the next choice a place to stand.
